western_tropical.label: Western Tropical

mother.notes: Primary nurturer; modern reading may reassign to whichever parent was more home-oriented.

father.notes: Authority/legacy figure; modern reading may reassign to the more dominant or boundary-setting parent.

siblings.notes: Includes cousins and the childhood peer/neighborhood environment.

children.notes: 5th house = first child. Subsequent children traditionally read from houses 5+2n (7th, 9th, ...).

spouse.notes: Descendant axis. Committed partnership, legal contracts, the 'other' in close relationship.

general_lineage.notes: Accumulated family wealth/values, inherited speech patterns, early upbringing tone.

western_tropical.notes: Sullivan's 'water houses' framework: 4th (roots), 8th (inherited trauma/resources), 12th (unconscious/hidden family material).

vedic.label: Vedic / Jyotish

father.notes: Some traditional systems use the 5th house instead of the 9th.

siblings.notes: 3rd house = younger siblings; 11th house = older siblings and extended social network.

general_lineage.notes: Family wealth, lineage, speech, and immediate upbringing.

vedic.notes: Same water-house logic applies, though some traditional Vedic schools weight the 9th (father/dharma/lineage) more heavily for ancestral material than the 8th.

planetary_thread_rules.description: Rules for detecting recurring planetary combinations ('threads') across family members, per Lynn Bell's genogram method.

planet_filtering.notes: Generational planets move slowly enough (84-248yr orbits) that any two people born within a few years of each other will share sign/aspect placements regardless of family relation, which is generational noise, not family-specific signal. Excluded from the thread detector by default; that signal belongs to the separate generational_cohort_lens feature instead. Expose as an opt-in toggle (label results 'generational' vs 'personal' thread) rather than a hard rule, in case users want to see them anyway.

planetary_thread_rules.notes: A thread is flagged when the same planet-pair + aspect-type combination (e.g., Moon-Pluto square) appears in 2 or more family members' natal charts, independent of house placement. Restrict planet-pair combinations to the included_by_default set unless the caller opts in to generational_planets.

family_element_profile_rules.description: Weighting rules for aggregating elemental (Fire/Earth/Air/Water) balance across a person's chart and across a family, per Sullivan's family element typing.
family_element_profile_rules.notes: Sun, Moon, and Ascendant are weighted double relative to the other 8 planets, since they conventionally dominate a chart's felt temperament more than e.g. Uranus's sign (which mostly reflects generation, not individual character -- the same generational-noise concern as planetary_thread_rules.planet_filtering). Ascendant is excluded entirely when houses_reliable is false (unknown birth time defaulted to noon), since Ascendant sign changes roughly every two hours and a noon-default chart's Ascendant carries no real signal. This weighting is a design decision, not an established astrological standard -- reasonable astrologers could weight this differently; revisit if family archetype output feels off.

family_timeline_rules.description: Rules for the family timeline: life events by age per person, and cross-generational age-timing coincidences, per Lynn Bell's family timing/anniversary method.
family_timeline_rules.notes: A timing pattern is flagged when 2+ family members experience the same event_type at the exact same age (completed years, computed from birth_date to event_date). This is exact-age matching only, not a tolerance band (e.g., age 46 vs 47 do not match) -- a fuzzy version was deliberately left unbuilt rather than shipped half-working; revisit with a documented tolerance rule if real family data shows near-miss patterns worth capturing. event_type is a fixed, config-driven taxonomy (not free text) so that cross-person matching is meaningful -- two people's free-text descriptions of 'similar' events would rarely match exactly.
